nodes.text: You've the look of somebody who's been north. Then you'll know what the caravans are shouting — the Masons' Guild broke their own seal. The *Undercroft* is open again. Twenty years shut, and open again.

I swung my first hammer down there, under the mountain. Grand Forge apprentice, me and *Balla* both, fighting over the same anvil like cats over a windowsill. Then the kobolds came up through the deep galleries, and the Guild closed the whole district with my father's crew still setting the last stones. He set stones the way I set edges — properly. _The seal was his._
So when the coal boys sing about starfall veins and open galleries, I hear a door my father built being propped open with his own chisel. That's all the story. What do you want at my forge?

choices.text: Would you ever go back up?

nodes.text: Balla's asked. Every solstice letter, one line at the bottom: *the anvil's still here*. Maybe now the door's open I'll walk up and lose the trials again, once, for the look on her face. If you pass the Grand Forge before I do — tell her Bretta says her quenches always ran cold.
So am I, and I've had twenty years' practice at it. He'd have liked the town, I think. He always said stone should hold something — coin, bread, people. This one holds all three.
Schematics on the shelf, steel on the racks, and everything priced honest because I can't be bothered to haggle.
Right. Enough smoke without a fire under it. Come by the forge when you need steel or the knowing of it.
